title: SparseBitMatrix::matvec prefetch + block-CSR layout
description:
Add software prefetch and a block-CSR layout to `SparseBitMatrix::matvec`. Currently scalar CSR with no prefetch; the gather pattern is index-driven and cache-unfriendly for LDPC parity-check matrices.

## Background

`SparseBitMatrix::matvec` in `crates/gf2-core/src/sparse.rs` does scalar CSR iteration. No prefetch, no block layout. The gather pattern reads `col_idx[i]` and follows it into the input vector — a memory access pattern that misses L1 frequently for LDPC-sized matrices.

The fix walks PPC steps:

- V6 prefetch: software prefetch of `col_idx[i + lookahead]` while processing entry $i$. Tune `lookahead` from L1 latency.
- V7 layout: block-CSR with $4 \times 64$ dense bit-blocks within sparse rows. Add a one-shot transformer from CSR to block-CSR. The transformer is a separate function — callers opt in.
- V3 SIMD: only inside dense blocks (XOR-reduce a u64 row of 4 packed columns).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Bit-exact vs. existing CSR matvec.
- [hard] Block-CSR transformer is a separate function; existing CSR path unchanged for callers that do not opt in.
- [hard] Sibling `*.asm.txt` artefact shows prefetch instructions actually emitted.
- [hard] `perf stat -r 10` capture shows L1d-miss rate drops on the LDPC-sized sparse bench.
- [hard] Word-boundary `#[test]`s pass for the transformer.
- [aspirational] $\geq 1.5\times$ geomean on `sparse.rs` bench at LDPC parity-check sizes.

## Notes

Cache-bound kernel: rely on cache-miss-rate improvement when IPC delta is small but L1d-miss drops materially. Bench: `sparse` (existing, pinned by I1). Spec doc: `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`.
